Final Fantasy XIV preps for the Moonfire Faire while addressing load times on the Switch 2 version
Square Enix Deploys An Emergency Update To Fix Final Fantasy 14 Loading Times On The Switch 2
items.summary: Now you can die in your duty without worry
items.content:
The Switch 2 version of Final Fantasy XIV is great except for terrible load times. A new patch is here to fix that. Last night, the game underwent emergency maintenance to address a bug related to players’ screens going permanently dark during battle phase transitions in dungeons or when attempting to revive a K.O.’d player. It seems to have worked. Players are now reporting reduced loading times.

『FF14』Switch2版のロード時間が短縮。蘇生やクレセントアイルのロード時間はさらに短縮！

先ほどアップデートが配信され爆速で修正。ロード時間も爆速に。 #Switch2でFF14 https://t.co/qDbLoGl50c pic.twitter.com/i2qe8pFJCn

— はっち速報｜ゲーム情報・新作レビュー@Game8 (@Game8_news) August 7, 2026

There were also a couple of issues affecting Switch 2 players who use touch controls. Apparently, the game would mark players using touch controls in dungeons as inactive, removing them from the dungeon. There were also issues with touch control targeting in a Gold Saucer shooting mini-game. Both of those glitches have been addressed, as well. But while you can use the Switch 2 mouse controls to play FFXIV , it seems like the latest update hasn’t addressed the lag issues with doing so.

The emergency hotfix addressed a number of other problems not related to the Switch 2, however. You can check out the full patch notes here .

items.title: Final Fantasy XIV Online Updated On Switch 2, Here Are The Full Patch Notes
items.content:
Square Enix already gave us a handy heads up that it would address some loading issues with Final Fantasy XIV Online for the Switch 2.

Now, the update is live, but it brings a host of other improvements and fixes along with it, several of which are specifically for Nintendo's console. The loading is the highlight, of course, but we've also got improvements to touch screen functionality and more.

So make sure you update the game to the latest version manually if it doesn't do it automatically (and it really should). For now, here's a look at the full patch notes:

■ Optimised processing to speed up data loading to reduce the time of screen transitions within duties. (Nintendo Switch™ 2 version only) ■ The following issues have been addressed: - Upon completing the Allied Society Quest “Hero's Day Off,” a message notifying that your reputation had advanced to “Allied” would not appear. - In the Occult Crescent: North Horn, the quest "In the Shadow of the Tower" would display the quest completed icon above the NPC even if the objective had not been completed. - In the following duties, if a player logged out while incapacitated and then logged back in more than 10 minutes later, they could return to the duty despite having been expelled. - The Occult Crescent: South Horn - Forked Tower: Blood - The Occult Crescent: North Horn - Forked Tower: Magic - The Occult Crescent: North Horn - The Forked Tower: Magic (Extreme) - The Forbidden Land, Eureka Hydatos - The Baldesion Arsenal - In the Occult Crescent, when a player had multiple damage-nullifying buffs from the following phantom actions, receiving damage would not only consume the buff of the corresponding damage type, but other damage-nullifying buffs as well. Shirahadori / Image / Occult Blink - In the Occult Crescent: North Horn critical encounter “Dark Artistry,” the visual effect of the enemy action “Dark Flare” appeared narrower than the actual attack. - In the Occult Crescent: North Horn critical encounter “Accept No Imitators,” no sound effect was played when the visual indicator for the boss action “Spinebreaking Stampede” was displayed. - In the Occult Crescent: North Horn FATE “Eye to Eye,” certain visual effects from the boss actions ”Cold Stare” and “Sinister Sight” were displayed for players who were not participating in the FATE. - In the Occult Crescent: North Horn, stepping onto the circles to travel to specific locations could cause players to become stuck in the ground or midair and prevent movement. - The animations/visual effects for the following phantom actions were not displayed properly in the Occult Crescent. Occult Aero III / Occult Holy / Chaos Drive / Punishing Ray / Drain Touch / Step Forth - Visual effects were not depicted properly at certain camera angles for the following weapons when they were drawn. Phantom Spear Occultum / Phantom Cane Occultum / Phantom Index Occultum / Phantom Codex Occultum / Phantom Revolver Occultum / Phantom Degen Occultum - When Tradewinds Gaskins were equipped along with certain foot gear on the following races/genders, graphics around the waist were displayed incorrectly: Midlander Male / Highlander Male / Elezen Male / Miqo'te Male / Au Ra Male / Viera Male - When Vana'dielian Tights of Healing were equipped on the following races/genders, the graphics of the left leg were displayed incorrectly when an idle animation entered a specific pose: Midlander Female / Highlander Female / Elezen Female / Viera Female - The keybind and log filter settings saved via Configuration Sharing were stored under "Miscellaneous Data" instead of "Character Configuration." - Touch screen input was not recognised as player input during duties, causing players using only touch screen controls to be treated as inactive and forcibly removed from duties after a certain period of time. (Nintendo Switch™ 2 version only) - In the Gold Saucer GATE "Air Force One", shots fired via touch screen controls were launched toward the previous reticle position rather than the location touched. (Nintendo Switch™ 2 version only) - Duty Recorder replay data did not play back correctly when a chapter was selected while the replay was paused. (Nintendo Switch™ 2 version only)

We're still busy tinkering away at our review for Final Fantasy XIV Online, so if you're on the fence about this one, then be sure to check it out when it's live.

items.title: 'Final Fantasy 14' Devs Working on a Fix for Switch 2's 'Unacceptable' Load Times
items.summary: Players have been reporting game-breaking load times that make high-end content nearly impossible
items.content:
on Google Preferred Source Google News Link copied to clipboard By Willa Rowe Published Aug 5, 2026, 1:18 PM EDT News The new platform launch still has some kinks to work out

FFXIV Evercold will finally modernize some of the MMO's most outdated features Game Freak promises to fix Beast of Reincarnation with 'continuous updates' after rocky launch Marvel Rivals to shrink file size 'without sacrificing a single pixel of visual fidelity' Final Fantasy 14 team says it's working on Switch 2 port's 'unacceptable' load times Final Fantasy 14 Sign in to your Polygon.com account Square Enix finally released Final Fantasy 14 on Nintendo Switch 2 this week, and the game's one-month early access period on the new platform has gone fairly smoothly but is not without problems. One of the biggest issues players are encountering is slow load times. The day after launch, Square Enix says a fix is in the works.

Players began reporting the issue only hours after Final Fantasy 14 became available on Switch 2. One post on Reddit described getting stuck on a black screen for nearly 20 seconds while being revived during eight-player content (such as trials and normal raids). That's a major problem for high-end content that includes enrage timers, a mechanic that wipes an entire party if an encounter is not completed within a certain time limit. Because of this, the poster called the load times on Switch 2 "unacceptable."

To Square Enix's credit, the company identified the issue soon after it began popping up. According to an official post on Final Fantasy 14 's the Lodestone website, the team confirmed that the issue seems to be focused on instanced duties and is triggered "when a player enters an instanced duty while surrounded by many characters." As players tend to queue for duties while in crowded areas such as Aetheryte plazas , the issue has the potential to be widespread. The post also notes that once the problem starts, it doesn't stop until after the duty in question is finished, which is especially troublesome.

Square Enix has identified the data reloading and cache clearing processes as potential culprits, and is working on a fix. The plan is to optimize the processes in question to ensure faster load times. An updated version with these fixes is currently in testing, and Square Enix says it will release the fix as soon as possible. Players can check the Lodestone for the latest updates on a potential fix. Until then, players can try to queue for duties in low-traffic areas to avoid the issue.

items.title: Final Fantasy XIV on Switch 2 is Better Than Anyone Expected
items.summary: Final Fantasy XIV is shaping up to be one of the Switch 2's most technically ambitious ports, with Square Enix targeting stable performance while bringing the full MMORPG experience to Nintendo's latest hybrid console.
items.content:
Final Fantasy XIV is shaping up to be one of the Switch 2's most technically ambitious ports, with Square Enix targeting stable performance while bringing the full MMORPG experience to Nintendo's latest hybrid console.

When Final Fantasy XIV was first announced for Nintendo Switch 2, skepticism was understandable. This is, after all, an MMORPG that has been evolving continuously for more than a decade. It spans multiple expansions, supports hundreds of players in shared social spaces, features massive raids, sprawling cities, and some of the busiest online hubs in gaming.

Translating all of that to a handheld system seemed like an enormous technical challenge. But it's clear that Square Enix seems to be taking on the task very seriously based on our early impressions of the game so far today at launch.

Producer and director Naoki Yoshida (Yoshi-P) has confirmed that the team has prioritized consistent performance over raw frame rate, targeting a stable 30 FPS throughout the majority of gameplay . Rather than chasing higher numbers, the focus has been on maintaining smooth combat and reliable frame pacing during the content players spend most of their time enjoying things like main scenario quests, dungeons, trials, raids, crafting, gathering, and exploration.

"I want to be honest with you: we are working really hard on the optimisation. We are striving to get the best performance. I think with the towns, you may see a lower framerate, only because there are so many players that are rendered on the screen.

The Nintendo Switch 2 is a wonderful console, and I think you can choose the way you want to play. You are more free to choose which mode to play in, so I hope that players will find the way to play that is most suited for themselves."

- Naoki Yoshida (Yoshi-P), game director, during a press conference

Cities like Limsa Lominsa regularly fill with hundreds of player characters showing off mounts, glamour sets, minions, and particle-heavy abilities. Even on significantly more powerful hardware, those areas have historically been among the game's toughest rendering scenarios. Square Enix has been transparent that these locations are where Switch 2 players are most likely to see performance fluctuate, but the team says it has spent considerable time optimizing the experience leading up to launch.

From the time I've spent with the game so far, you can definitely feel the impact. But since these are social gathering areas or just dialogue- and menu-heavy environments, it's not really a big detractor from gameplay. When you're outside of the city doing quests or in an instance, it's been very smooth so far.

I picked up playing with my level 30 Gladiator I abandoned a few years ago on PC, so it's been a little bit of a learning curve so far. Fortunately, if you really want to, you don't have to play in handheld mode or using a controller since there's mouse support on Switch 2, including both USB options and the Joy-Con's mouse mode.

"As everyone already knows, the Nintendo Switch 2 is an amazing piece of hardware. If you place it in the dock, you can play in TV mode. If you use it in Portable mode, you can carry it and play it at your leisure. For example, when challenging a high-difficulty Raid, you can play on TV while connecting a mouse and keyboard, and then you can craft and gather while in Portable mode. I feel like this will enable a play style that is unique to Nintendo Switch 2.

Following the announcement at the keynote speech, I also saw some voices on social media asking, 'Is it going to be alright spec-wise?', but we are thoroughly optimizing it. There are no performance issues at all during actual content. It's much more hectic when you're in a town with a lot of characters, though I think it should run stably around 30 frames there as well. The performance is better in the actual content, so I think it should be okay, and you should not worry."

- Naoki Yoshida (Yoshi-P), game director, in an interview with Famitsu reported by RPGSite

Unlike many MMORPG adaptations, this isn't a separate handheld version with isolated servers or reduced functionality. Switch 2 players log into the same persistent world as everyone else across PC, PlayStation, and Xbox. Every expansion, every raid, every social space, every seasonal event, and every update arrives together, allowing players to seamlessly continue their existing characters wherever they choose to play in both handheld and docked modes.

Here’s the lineup of pricing: Starter Edition – $19.99 Complete Edition – $59.99 ($41.99 with pre-orders) Complete Collector’s Edition – $139.99 ($97.99 with pre-orders) Dawntrail Expansion (requires base...
items.content:
At the 2026 Final Fantasy 14 Fan Festival in Berlin today, Square Enix revealed the release date for the MMORPG on Nintendo Switch 2. It will be out on August 4, 2026.

That was just one piece of news we got today. Square Enix also unveiled a Final Fantasy 7 Remake Trilogy crossover raid series and more.

Square Enix today revealed brand-new information about Evercold, the sixth expansion for its critically acclaimed MMORPG Final Fantasy 14 Online, set to launch in January 2027 alongside new playable content, a Final Fantasy 7 Remake Trilogy crossover raid series, the Nintendo Switch 2 version release date and more.

An extended teaser trailer for Evercold was also revealed, providing a glimpse into the world of the Fourth and the adventures that await the Warrior of Light in the start of the Goddless Realms Saga story arc.

During the Fan Festival 2026 in Berlin keynote address, Producer and Director Naoki Yoshida revealed the first new job coming to Evercold: Bastion—a main tank that wields a pair of greatshields known as skyltborg—and unveiled a trailer showcasing the new job in action.

Details were also shared on several new features coming to Evercold, including changes to the narrative structure that will be implemented for the main scenario, field, and game system, allowing players more freedom to choose what area they complete first between various paths in the main scenario. Through Auto Content Balancing, difficulty scaling and enemy levels will adjust to the appropriate player level as they play through dungeons in their chosen order. Additionally, a first look was provided for Character Action Skins, a feature that lets players assign alternate animations to personalize existing General actions, such as Teleport and Warp, with support for additional skins such as job actions arriving in future updates. Character customization will also be expanded so players have more ways to make their character stand out, including a greater range of color options with the new color picker, the ability to fine-tune features such as eyes and lips, new elements such as eye shadow, and more.

Following the reveal of the EVANGELION – Ghosts of Desire alliance raid series in April, Yoshida unveiled a new teaser trailer and announced that acclaimed director and animator Mahiro Maeda will join the project as a special guest artist and designer. Throughout his career, Maeda has contributed to numerous acclaimed projects, including “Mad Max: Fury Road” (2015) as a concept artist and designer, and “EVANGELION:3.0 +1.0 THRICE UPON A TIME” (2021), where he served as director, concept art director, storyboard artist, art setting designer and key animator.

Joined on stage by Final Fantasy 7 Remake series Director Naoki Hamaguchi, Yoshida also revealed “Beyond the Lifestream,” a new Final Fantasy 7-themed 8-player raid series that players will challenge in Evercold. Both development teams are working closely together to create an exciting new raid experience for players.

Further, Final Fantasy 14 will launch on Nintendo Switch 2 on Tuesday, August 4, 2026, with pre-orders starting today on Nintendo eShop. To ensure server stability, there will be an approximately one-month free subscription period on Nintendo Switch 2. Whether beginning with the Free Trial, starting their adventure with the Starter Edition, or diving into the full story and experience with the Complete Edition, more players than ever before will soon be able to join together in the vast world of Final Fantasy 14.

An outline of the content reveals from the keynote address can be found below:

Finally, Yoshida revealed the Evercold Collector’s Bundle, which includes a collection of physical items: the Evercold Special Art Box, Expertly Crafted Reaper Figure, Ethos Metal Keychain, Köttr Mini Plush, and Tapestry of the Fourth. Also included is the digital Collector’s Edition, featuring three in-game items: the Crystal Skyltborg bastion weapon, Vallhallar Odin mount, and Entreat Crystal emote. More information regarding availability and pre-orders will be announced in the future.
